subject: Re: Long-context evals / recommended models and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Romero <alice.romero@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Long-context evals — follow-up and proposed next steps

Hi Alice — great to meet you and the ACME team this morning. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we can move toward a short POC focused on long-context summarization fidelity and truncation behavior:

- Scope we agreed: ingest batches of ~200–500 customer-support conversations (avg token length ~25k) to evaluate summarization fidelity and behavior past 32k windows.
- Key success metrics: summary ROUGE/ROUGE-L / semantic similarity vs. human baseline; fraction of summaries with hallucinations; truncation failure rate; latency at 95th percentile.
- Immediate asks from ACME: sample dataset + privacy redaction rules; list of prompt variants you want us to test.

What we (Redwood) will deliver in the initial eval (2 weeks):
- Baseline runs across 3 model families (open Llama-2 variants, Mistral-like, and a 70B quantized variant we host) with recommended prompt sets.
- Benchmarks: readability/faithfulness report, observed truncation points, and token-level cost estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated.
- Concrete suggestions: batching/cache settings, quantization profile, and whether to route long jobs to Dedicated for cost predictability.

I've attached a short recommendation sheet and the prompt set we typically start with for these tests. Rishi and Nikhil are copied — Rishi will own model selection and benchmarking; Nikhil will help with dataset ingest and privacy rules.

Next steps: please send sample dataset (or a sanitized subset) and confirm whether you want us to include a 100k-token extreme-case test. If we get materials by Friday (03/06), we can kick-off the eval next Monday.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment(s): redwood-recommendation-sheet.pdf, prompt_set_acme_v2.jsonl

Hi Alice — great, thanks. Quick note on model recommendations and telemetry so we align on the comparability tests:

Model slate I recommend for the first pass (we can expand after initial results):
1) redwood-lc-70b-q4 (our quantized 70B variant) — best balance of fidelity/cost for 50–100k tokens.
2) open-llama-34b-highcontext — native large-context variant with good summarization heuristics.
3) brisk-13b-xxl (Mistral-family style) — lower cost; useful as a cost/latency baseline.

Comparability tests (we'll run these against your acme-prod-1):
- Exact prompt/seeded sampling to compare outputs on the same input.
- ROUGE / BERTScore / embedding-similarity to human summaries.
- Hallucination checks: named-entity drift and factual consistency heuristics.
- Truncation diagnostics: identify token offsets where KV cache misses or forced truncation changed outputs.

Telemetry we'd like for the POC (please confirm availability):
- Read-only S3 link to sample inputs (yes/no)
- Ground-truth human summaries for a 50-item subset (high priority)
- Any current tokenization and chunking scripts you use

Links I uploaded for initial benchmarking methodology and prompt templates:
- Long-context benchmark playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-eval
- Prompt templates and evaluation harness (example): https://redwood-internal.s3/benchmarks/long_context_summary.html

I'll queue the baseline runs once we have the sample and the ground-truth subset. Marissa — want me to produce a short one-page model recommendation sheet (latency/cost/expected fidelity) for ACME leadership?

— Rishi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Long-context evals — follow-up and proposed next steps

Great — thanks for the fast turnaround, Alice. Short answers to your questions and the plan below:

- Quantization profile: for redwood-lc-70b-q4 we typically start with Q4_0 for Hosted evaluation (lower-upfront engineering) and Q4_K_Mix for Dedicated (better fidelity at minimal extra cost). I'll have Rishi include the exact profile names in his one-page sheet.
- Truncation fallback: our recommended default is automatic prefix-KV caching with a two-pass summarization: (1) chunk-and-summarize segments with overlap, (2) summarize summaries to preserve coherence. For extreme cases we can run a sliding-window fidelity pass that highlights sections dropped by truncation and produces a confidence score. We'll include these as part of the deliverables.

Immediate next steps (plan):
1) ACME: upload sanitized sample and tokenization scripts to S3 by 2026-03-05 EOD.
2) Redwood: baseline runs across 3 models + one comparability run vs acme-prod-1 (start 2026-03-09).
3) Redwood: deliver interim results and recommendation sheet by 2026-03-16.
4) Decision: leadership review and procurement conversation week of 2026-03-23.

I'll add the timeline to the HubSpot deal and kick off the eval project once files arrive. Thanks again — attaching the initial eval results template (spreadsheet) so you can see the fields we'll populate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
